summary: This is a Mol Labs public hypothesis card (N15) proposing a pre-registered sleep-deprivation psychomotor vigilance (PVT) experiment to test whether modafinil's alertness benefit survives a selective DAT-inhibitor arm occupancy-matched to published PET figures (~50% striatal DAT occupancy). The document is a research discussion/proposal at TRL 1, with no experiments run, framing an "assumption-kill" of the DAT-sufficiency hypothesis for modafinil's PVT effect. All experimental evidence cited is from existing literature (Volkow, Kim, Wesensten), and the key matched residual-PVT panel is explicitly marked UNKNOWN and NOT_RUN.

content_blocks.title: Claim / Hypothesis Statement (N15)
content_blocks.content: On a pre-registered sleep-deprivation psychomotor vigilance (PVT) panel with three arms — (1) a selective DAT inhibitor occupancy-matched to Volkow/Kim modafinil striatal DAT (~50% caudate/putamen), (2) a methylphenidate-class positive-control arm, and (3) a modafinil arm — the prediction is that under the DAT-matched selective DAT-i condition that abolishes methylphenidate-class ΔPVT, modafinil retains residual ΔPVT ≥50% of modafinil-alone ΔPVT (ms mean RT or lapses/trial; α/N pre-specified). This is labeled an 'assumption-kill / dat-insufficiency' hypothesis.

content_blocks.title: Scientific Rationale / Why It Matters
content_blocks.content: Popular and PET framing treat ~50% striatal DAT occupancy as sufficient to explain modafinil alertness/PVT. N15 asks whether residual modafinil ΔPVT survives a DAT-matched block that kills a DAT-primary stimulant PVT arm. Distinct from N1 (DAT-alone vs H3/orexin variance wording; 0 DAT×PVT mediation) — N15 is specifically about residual modafinil ΔPVT under occupancy-matched selective DAT-i that abolishes methylphenidate-class PVT. Occupancy PET (Volkow/Kim) and modafinil PVT (Wesensten) are separate literature; no co-designed abolish×residual panel exists.

content_blocks.title: Mechanism Sketch
content_blocks.content: DAT-insufficiency assumption-kill: Human PET shows modafinil occupies striatal DAT (~40–57%; Volkow [11C]cocaine; Kim [18F]FE-PE2I). Separate sleep-deprivation panels show modafinil PVT/alertness gain (Wesensten). No published head-to-head scores residual modafinil ΔPVT under a selective DAT-i arm occupancy-matched to those PET figures that abolishes methylphenidate-class PVT. Optional H3 inverse-agonist parallel arm is adjacent only (Parmentier/Lin; discard H3 'block' identity). Competing caveats: occupancy mismatch / MPH positive-control failure for PK reasons / underpowered sleep-debt strata leave the test inconclusive rather than refuted.

content_blocks.title: Prior Art / Literature Evidence
content_blocks.content:
1. PMID 19293415 (Volkow et al., JAMA 2009): Human PET [11C]cocaine DAT occupancy after oral modafinil — caudate ~53.8%, putamen ~47.2%, NAcc ~39.3%. Defines occupancy match target; not residual-PVT under DAT-matched block H2H.
2. PMID 24451483 (Kim et al.): Human PET DAT-selective [18F]FE-PE2I striatal occupancy ~51.4% (200 mg) / ~56.9% (300 mg). Independent match point; not residual-PVT H2H.
3. PMID 16120100 (Wesensten 2005, DOI 10.1111/j.1365-2869.2005.00468.x): Sleep-deprivation PVT/alertness panel — modafinil restores performance vs placebo (vs caffeine / d-amphetamine). Modafinil PVT prior; not DAT-matched block residual-PVT H2H.
4. PMID 17288995 (Parmentier/Lin 2007): H3 inverse-agonist class vs modafinil / HDC KO wake persistence; tiprolisant+modafinil synergy implies parallel not identity — optional adjacent arm only; not DAT-matched residual-PVT H2H.

content_blocks.content:

content_blocks.title: Baseline Measured vs. Unknown
content_blocks.content:
MEASURED (literature): Modafinil striatal DAT occupancy (PMID 19293415; 24451483). Modafinil PVT/alertness under sleep deprivation (PMID 16120100). H3 class adjacent literature (PMID 17288995).
UNKNOWN: Matched residual-modafinil-ΔPVT under selective DAT-i occupancy-matched to Volkow/Kim that abolishes methylphenidate-class PVT. Soft-complete modafinil∩DAT∩PVT∩(MPH|occupancy) = 0; MPH∩PVT∩(occupancy|DAT) = 0. Token NON-MATCHes: ICSS 28125506, review 28740389, fatigue 22776872.
PREDICTION: Residual modafinil ΔPVT ≥50% of modafinil-alone when MPH ΔPVT abolished.

content_blocks.title: Actionable Limitations
content_blocks.content:
1. Do not treat N1–N14 as proving N15 — N1 is DAT-alone vs H3/orexin variance wording with 0 DAT×PVT mediation hits; that emptiness is not a DAT-matched block residual-PVT panel; soft-complete empty ≠ demonstrated residual gain.
2. Occupancy PET ≠ PVT abolish panel — Volkow/Kim measure DAT occupancy; Wesensten measures modafinil PVT under sleep deprivation; none co-designs selective DAT-i occupancy-matched abolish of MPH PVT with residual modafinil readout.
3. H3 adjacent ≠ DAT-matched design; discard H3 'block' identity; positive-control MPH∩PVT∩occupancy literature sparse (tight = 0); include MPH-class PVT positive control under same DAT condition; no dosing; NOT MB/MAOI.

content_blocks.title: Refutation Criteria
content_blocks.content: On the pre-registered sleep-deprivation PVT panel, under the selective DAT-i arm occupancy-matched to Volkow/Kim that abolishes methylphenidate-class ΔPVT, residual modafinil ΔPVT falls below 50% of modafinil-alone ΔPVT (ms mean RT or lapses/trial) — so DAT-sufficiency / DAT-primary framing for modafinil PVT survives and dat-insufficiency fails — when occupancy-match, MPH abolish-gate, and power artifacts that would otherwise leave the test inconclusive are ruled out.

content_blocks.title: Ablation Analysis
content_blocks.content:
Three critical components identified whose removal would invalidate the hypothesis test:
1. Remove same sleep-deprivation PVT contrast of residual modafinil ΔPVT under selective DAT-i occupancy-matched to Volkow/Kim that abolishes methylphenidate-class ΔPVT → separate DAT-occupancy LITERATURE and modafinil-PVT LITERATURE cannot show dat-insufficiency.
2. Remove occupancy-matched selective DAT-i identity (Volkow/Kim striatal DAT match) plus MPH-class abolish gate → residual modafinil PVT is just 'another wake drug under nonspecific block,' not an assumption-kill of DAT-sufficiency.
3. Remove N1≠this + N1–N14≠proof + soft-complete-empty≠novelty + H3-identity-discarded + occupancy-PET≠PVT-abolish-panel discipline → treating N1 mediation emptiness, H3 adjacent priors, or Volkow/Kim/Wesensten alone as already deciding residual modafinil PVT would invent an H2H result left UNKNOWN.

key_findings: Hypothesis N15 is at TRL 1 (concept/proposal only): execution_status=NOT_RUN, no experiments performed.

Modafinil occupies striatal DAT at ~40–57% (caudate ~53.8%, putamen ~47.2%, NAcc ~39.3% per Volkow PMID 19293415; striatum ~51.4–56.9% per Kim PMID 24451483) — these are the occupancy match targets for the proposed experiment.
Modafinil restores PVT performance under sleep deprivation vs placebo (Wesensten 2005, PMID 16120100) — established literature baseline, not a new experiment.

The key experimental variable — matched residual modafinil ΔPVT under selective DAT-i occupancy-matched to Volkow/Kim that abolishes methylphenidate-class PVT — is explicitly UNKNOWN (soft-complete search = 0 hits).
Prediction: residual modafinil ΔPVT ≥50% of modafinil-alone ΔPVT (ms mean RT or lapses/trial) while MPH-class ΔPVT ≤0 under the same DAT-matched selective DAT-i.
Refutation criterion: residual modafinil ΔPVT <50% of modafinil-alone ΔPVT under the same conditions would support DAT-sufficiency framing.
Estimated time to refute: 4 weeks; kill_cost_tier=1; ip_class=dat-insufficiency; vault_hold=no.
H3 inverse-agonist arm (tiprolisant+modafinil synergy, PMID 17288995) is adjacent/optional only — H3 'block' identity explicitly discarded.
No dosing specified; NOT MB/MAOI; FTO status UNKNOWN.
Status label: NEGATIVE (polarity: negative); novelty_tag: assumption-kill; no prior art found for the specific H2H abolish×residual panel design.
